title: Lena and the Orbit
premise: Kestrel Hartwell investigates impossible accidents for an insurance consortium that insures the shipping lanes between two colonies severed by a decades-old war. When the children of both colonies begin dreaming the same dream — a signal from the derelict relay at the edge of dead space — Kestrel discovers his late mother helped build that relay, and that the 'accidents' he's been investigating were cover-ups to keep it silent. Racing a rival salvage crew and his own employer's enforcers, he reaches the relay and finds it carrying a recorded peace offer from the war's last hours, suppressed because peace would bankrupt the insurers. In the end Kestrel broadcasts the truth at the cost of his career and nearly his life, choosing loyalty to the dead over obedience to the living — and opening a channel between worlds that finally begin to speak.
about_author: Lior Eastwick is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who spent eleven years investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town where the fog comes in on schedule, like a signal.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Kestrel Hartwell closes a routine claim aboard a freighter running the silence between rival colonies Meridian and Calloway, establishing his methodical voice and the political cold war framing his work. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: competent loneliness, a man at home in transit and nowhere else.

chapters.title: Impossible Numbers
chapters.summary: Back at the consortium office, Kestrel flags three accidents whose insurance payouts trace to the same shell account. His supervisor, Vess, urges him to close the file. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: the first itch of doubt — the numbers don't lie, but people do.

chapters.title: Children of Two Worlds
chapters.summary: On Meridian, teacher Amara Osei notices her students drawing identical images: a tower of light in darkness. On Calloway, a boy wakes screaming the same coordinates. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear as the dream spreads across enemy lines.

chapters.title: The Claim That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Kestrel interviews a widow whose husband died near dead space; she slips him her husband's logbook, which mentions 'the relay singing.' POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into resolve; the case turns personal.

chapters.title: Mother's Blueprints
chapters.summary: Sorting his mother's estate, Kestrel finds engineering schematics bearing her signature — for the very relay at the edge of dead space, officially never built. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden; the past reaches through paper.

chapters.title: Vess Closes Doors
chapters.summary: Consortium enforcers raid Kestrel's office; Vess warns him off with genuine regret, revealing the insurer's reach. Kestrel goes dark, buying passage on a smuggler's hauler. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: betrayal by institution, loyalty tested against survival.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Bargain
chapters.summary: Captain Idris Fen agrees to carry Kestrel toward dead space — for a price and a share of whatever the relay holds. Rival salvage crew the Corvid is already outbound. POV: Idris. Emotional beat: wary alliance; greed and curiosity sharing a cockpit.

chapters.title: What the Children Know
chapters.summary: Amara smuggles herself off Meridian with a child dreamer, Juno, who navigates by the dream itself. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: protective love outranking law; a teacher becomes a fugitive.

chapters.title: Dead Space Rules
chapters.summary: In the silence beyond navigation beacons, the hauler's systems fail one by one — exactly as the accidents did. Kestrel realizes the relay doesn't just broadcast; it interferes. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into understanding.

chapters.title: Juno's Map
chapters.summary: Idris's ship and Amara's escape pod converge; Juno guides them through a debris field no chart survives. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: the innocence of children as compass; trust across strangers.

chapters.title: The Corvid Closes
chapters.summary: The rival salvage crew boards under parley flag, led by Sable Renn, who once loved Kestrel and now works for the consortium. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: old love versus new orders; the theme of love against duty made flesh.

chapters.title: Halfway Ghosts
chapters.summary: Trapped together during a reactor scare, Kestrel and Sable trade truths about the war, their mothers, and what the consortium buried. POV: alternating Kestrel/Sable. Emotional beat: intimacy rekindled inside mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: The Relay Appears
chapters.summary: Out of nothing, the relay resolves — vast, ancient, still lit after forty years, running on power no one can explain. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: awe; the impossible made structural.

chapters.title: Inside Her Work
chapters.summary: Kestrel walks corridors built from his mother's blueprints, finding her final logs: the relay captured a last-ditch peace transmission from both colonies' leaders before the blackout order. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: communion with the dead; grief transmuted to purpose.

chapters.title: The Suppression Order
chapters.summary: Sable arrives with consortium authority: destroy the relay, collect the bounty, erase the transmission. She hesitates when Juno recites the dream aloud — the relay has been teaching the children, patiently, for years. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: duty cracking against conscience.

chapters.title: Signal vs. Silence
chapters.summary: The Corvid opens fire on the relay's antenna array while Vess's enforcement ship enters orbit above. Kestrel must choose: save the archive or save the people. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: sacrifice crystallizing; loyalty redefined.

chapters.title: Climb the Tower of Light
chapters.summary: Kestrel ascends the damaged spire to hand-broadcast the transmission, reliving his mother's climb in reverse. Sable defects mid-assault, holding the corridor. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: climax — love, truth, and inheritance fused into one act of defiance.

chapters.title: The Peace Recording
chapters.summary: The transmission plays across both colonies: the war's final hours, both leaders begging for ceasefire, silenced by profit. The dreams stop; the children wake speaking plainly. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: catharsis; truth landing like sunrise.

chapters.title: Cost Accounting
chapters.summary: Vess stands down rather than fire on witnesses; the consortium fractures as its own adjusters audit the shell accounts Kestrel exposed. Kestrel drifts wounded in the relay's shadow. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: institutional reckoning; a bureaucrat's quiet defection.

chapters.title: Two Voices on One Channel
chapters.summary: Meridian and Calloway open direct contact for the first time in decades; Amara's students exchange messages with the children they dreamed beside. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: reconciliation beginning small, human, real.

chapters.title: Claims Settled
chapters.summary: Kestrel, recovering, declines reinstatement and instead files one last claim — against the consortium itself — with Sable as witness and Idris as courier. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: justice as paperwork; the investigator becomes the claim.

chapters.title: Lena and the Orbit
chapters.summary: Revealed at last: Lena was Kestrel's mother's name, and the relay's designation — the orbit she gave her life to guard. Kestrel leaves the relay singing, takes the long route home between worlds that now speak. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: resolution — inheritance honored, loneliness answered, the orbit held.
